<h>Invitatorium</h>
<r>Ant.</r> Prope est iam Dóminus, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Prope est iam Dóminus, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>V</c>eníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
<r>Ant.</r> Prope est iam Dóminus, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius <n>(genuflectitur)</n> veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
<r>Ant.</r> Prope est iam Dóminus, * Veníte, adorémus.
<c>H</c>ódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<c>Q</c>uadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
<r>Ant.</r> Prope est iam Dóminus, * Veníte, adorémus.
<r>℣.</r> Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
<r>℟.</r> Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> Veníte, adorémus.
<r>Ant.</r> Prope est iam Dóminus, * Veníte, adorémus.

<h>Invitatory</h>
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is now near * O come, let us adore Him.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is now near * O come, let us adore Him.
<c>C</c>ome let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is now near * O come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>or the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. <n>(genuflect)</n> Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is now near * O come, let us adore Him.
<c>T</c>oday if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us adore Him.
<c>F</c>orty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.
<r>Ant.</r> The Lord is now near * O come, let us adore Him.
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.
<r>Ant.</r> O come, let us adore Him.

De Isaía Prophéta
<r>Isa 43:1-3</r>

<n>2</n> Cum transíeris per aquas, tecum ero, et flúmina non opérient te: cum ambuláveris in igne, non comburéris, et flamma non ardébit in te.
<n>3</n> Quia ego Dóminus Deus tuus sanctus Israël salvátor tuus, dedi propitiatiónem tuam Ægýptum, Æthiópiam, et Saba pro te.

<h>Martyrologium</h>
<c>Q</c>uintodécimo Kaléndas Ianuárii Luna nona. Anno Dómini 2026
<h>P</h>hilíppis, in Macedónia, natális sanctórum Mártyrum Rufi et Zósimi, qui ex illórum número discipulórum fuérunt, per quos primitíva Ecclésia in Iudǽis et Græcis fundáta est; de quorum étiam felíci agóne scribit sanctus Polycárpus in epístola ad Philippénses.
<h>L</h>aodicéæ, in Sýria, pássio sanctórum Theotími et Basiliáni.
<h>I</h>n Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Quincti, Simplícii et aliórum; qui sub Décii et Valeriáni persecutióne passi sunt.
<h>I</h>bídem sancti Moysétis Mártyris.
<h>I</h>tem in Africa sanctórum Mártyrum Victúri, Victóris, Victoríni, Adiutóris, Quarti et aliórum trigínta.
<h>M</h>opsuéstiæ, in Cilícia, sancti Auxéntii Epíscopi, qui, olim sub Licínio miles, pótius elégit cíngulum exúere quam uvas Baccho offérre; factúsque Epíscopus, præclárus méritis quiévit in pace.
<h>T</h>urónis, in Gállia, sancti Gratiáni Epíscopi, qui, a sancto Fabiáno Papa primus eiúsdem civitátis Epíscopus ordinátus est, et multis clarus miráculis obdormívit in Dómino.
<r>℣.</r> Et álibi aliórum plurimórum sanctórum Mártyrum et Confessórum, atque sanctárum Vírginum.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
b.79a1276b56:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>D</c>ecember 18th 2026, the 9th day of the Moon,
<h>O</h>n the morrow we keep the Feast of the Blessed Virgin Mary looking shortly to be delivered.
<h>U</h>pon the same 18th day of December, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Philippi, in Macedonia, (in the year 107,) the holy martyrs Rufus and Zozimus, who were of the number of the disciples by whom the early Church was founded among the Jews and Greeks of whose happy contending holy Polycarp writeth in his Epistle unto the Philippians.
<h>A</h>t Laodicea, in Syria, the holy martyrs Theotimus and Basilian.
<h>I</h>n Africa, the holy martyrs Quintus, Simplicius and others, who suffered in the persecution under the Emperors Decius and Valerian.
<h>T</h>here also the holy martyr Moysetes.
<h>L</h>ikewise in Africa also, the holy martyrs Victurus, Victor, Victorinus, Adjutor, Quartus, and thirty others.
<h>A</h>t Mopsuestia, in Cilicia, holy Auxentius, Bishop (of that see;) he was originally a soldier under the Emperor Licinius, but chose rather to cast away his military belt than to offer grapes to Bacchus; he afterwards became a Bishop, and fell asleep in peace, famous for worthy deeds, (fourth century.)
<h>A</h>t Tours, holy Bishop Gratian, who was ordained by holy Pope Fabian as the first Bishop of that city, and fell asleep in the Lord, famous for many miracles. (He was a disciple of the Apostles.)
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>A</c>urem tuam, quǽsumus, Dómine, précibus nostris accómmoda: et mentis nostræ ténebras, grátia tuæ visitatiónis illústra:
<h>Q</h>ui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre, in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.8c399da162:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> Lord, we beseech thee, mercifully incline thine ears unto our prayers, and lighten the darkness of our minds by the grace of thy heavenly visitation.
<h>W</h>ho livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
